lines.text: The model has never read Riya's college placement policy. So how does the bot answer from it, and even name the page?
The trick is RAG: retrieval-augmented generation. First retrieve the relevant text, then let the model generate from it. An open-book exam.
Phase one happens once, offline. Read the PDF, cut it into chunks, embed each chunk, and store the vectors with their page numbers.
Phase two runs on every question. Embed the question with the same model, and fetch the four nearest chunks.
Paste those chunks into the prompt, each with a number. Then add three rules: answer only from the context, cite the number, and if the answer isn't there, say you don't know.
The model answers, and cites chunk two. Your code maps that number back to page four, so anyone can check it.
Ask something the PDF can't answer, like the hostel wifi password, and a good bot refuses instead of inventing.
When an answer is wrong, print the retrieved chunks first. If the evidence never arrived, no prompt can fix it.
So remember: RAG doesn't train the model. It hands it the right page, at the right moment.
Next lesson: evaluating RAG, so you can prove it works.
